slides.eyebrow: A rule you'll wish you knew sooner
slides.sub: It's NJ's smoke and CO alarm certificate.

slides.title: It's on the seller
slides.body: Before a 1- or 2-family home is sold, leased or gets new occupants, the owner has to get this certificate from the local fire code enforcing agency.

slides.title: 10-year sealed batteries
slides.body: Battery smoke alarms have to be the 10-year sealed kind. Hardwired alarms can't be swapped out for battery ones.

slides.title: A CO alarm near the sleeping areas
slides.body: Homes with a fuel-burning device or an attached garage need a CO alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas.

slides.label: Fire extinguisher, within
slides.body: of the kitchen, rated at least 2A-10B:C and 10 pounds or less. Ask when the seller's inspection is booked. Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.

caption:
Here's a rule you'll wish you knew sooner: in NJ, the seller needs a fire safety certificate before you move in.

NJ's fire code says the owner of a 1- or 2-family home has to get a smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and fire extinguisher certificate before it's sold, leased or gets new occupants. Battery smoke alarms have to be the 10-year sealed kind. Homes with a fuel-burning device or an attached garage need a CO alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas. And there has to be a fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen.

Ask when the seller's inspection is booked so it doesn't hold up your move.

Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.
